The time complexity of binary search is O(log n), where n is the number of elements in the list being searched.

Binary search works by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half until the target value is found or the interval is empty. This process reduces the size of the search space with each iteration, making it more efficient than linear search (O(n)) for large lists. The logarithmic factor comes from the fact that the search space is halved at each step, which means the number of comparisons required grows logarithmically with the size of the input.
